newsitem.title: CANADA: BCE profit rises on Northern Telecom results.
newsitem.headline: BCE profit rises on Northern Telecom results.

text.p: Second-quarter profits at BCE Inc., Canada's largest telecommunications company, rose sharply on Wednesday on improved results from its Northern Telecom Ltd. subsidiary.

Montreal-based BCE, which is also Canada's most widely held company, said its net earnings rose to C$273 million ($199 million), or C43 cents (31 cents) a share, from year-earlier net income of C$206 million ($150 million), or C33 cents (24 cents) a share. Revenues jumped to C$8.1 billion ($5.9
billion) from C$6.7 billion ($4.9 billion) in the year-ago period.

BCE said its 51 percent-owned telecommunications equipment maker Northern Telecom contributed C$117 million ($85.4 million) to BCE's consolidated earnings, a 56 percent increase from C$75 million ($53 million) in last year's second quarter.
BCE's wholly owned Bell Canada, Canada's largest telephone company, contributed C$184 million ($134 million) of net income, vs. year-earlier C$169 million ($123 million).
But BCE said Bell Canada's return on equity of 10.2 percent was unsatisfactory, alhough it rose from 9.2 percent in the 1996 quarter.

Bell's local and access service revenues increased 10 percent from a year earlier, but its long-distance revenues were flat. At June 30, Bell's share of Canada's C$8 billion ($5.8 billion) long-distance telephone market was estimated at 66 percent, down from 71 percent at the end of lst year's second quarter, BCE said.

"In the first six months of the year, various factors, including intensifying competition and regulatory decisions, have increased the risks associated with Bell Canada's ability to meet its financial targets for the year," BCE said. Meeting those targets would remain a "significant challenge," the company said
In March, Bell lowered its 1997 profit forecast to C$850 million ($620 million) from C$950 million ($693 million).
BCE stock rose C20 cents to C$42.10 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday.
